decisions.reason: Conferencing is a commoditised, crowded market outside the firm's core network strengths, but it costs little to keep alongside the voice portfolio while its uptake remains unclear.
Concrete customer adoption for data centre and financial hub connectivity shows its value is being realised, which justifies further commitment rather than abandonment.
Optical spectrum is a growth area that fits the firm's core fibre network and already has a dedicated page, so it is an option worth keeping open while demand develops.
A self-service number ordering portal supports the existing voice business at low marginal cost, so keeping it is cheap even though its standalone value is uncertain.
Carrier pre-selection is a declining legacy service in a shrinking market, but some remaining customers and low upkeep costs make keeping it slightly more likely than an immediate drop within a year.
Direct voice interconnection is a core enterprise and wholesale offering on the existing network, cheap to maintain and still relevant as SIP migration continues.
